Klobuck Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kłobuck, Poland

Not demolished. Kłobuck, founded in the 13th century, saw permanent Jewish settlement develop in the first half of the 19th century, gaining an independent community by 1921; population grew from 15% (281) in 1827 to 25% (460) by 1850, reaching 2,001 members by 1937. A wartime ghetto (established October 1941, liquidated June 22, 1942) held 2,054 Jews before deportation to Auschwitz-Birkenau. This cemetery, established by the first half of the 19th century, was almost entirely destroyed by Germans, who used stolen matzevot to harden roads and pavements and build anti-tank obstacles; only one tombstone survives, commemorating Ryfka Korland (née Zygielbaum, d. December 10, 1933).
